Sources of available housing other than the existing market would be recently completed units; units under construction; units being planned; mobile homes ard Move-On units from areas where clearance is underway, such as the airport clear zone. The latter are structures that have been condemned and must be moved due to activities such as redevelopment or freeway construction, or implementation of airport land use regulations.
Experience of the Relocation Section indicates that displaced families generally elect to remain in or near their neighborhoods, particularly among their own language group. Due to the extensive redevelopment and clearance which has been underway in the San Jose area, decent, safe and sanitary housing, which is up to code, is becoming increasingly difficult to locate for those displaced by renewal activities. The Move-On program, as well as rehabilitation projects, are helping to alleviate the shortage.
B. GEOLOGY AND SOILS
Introduction
The discussion of the geologic and soil characteristics of San Jose in general, and the project sites, in particular, in Section II-B, demonstrated that there exist certain hazards in the areas proposed for the Block Grant program implementation. These physical hazards are the result of the geologic history of the San Jose area. The presence of potential earthquake faults and the proximity to active faults present one set of hazards. The alluvial nature of the Santa Clara Valley cause the problems of subsidence and various forms of ground failure. This section will examine each identified geologic problem and its potential impact upon each target neighborhood.
